newsitem.title: UK: Hong Kong to fall as top business location - survey.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong to fall as top business location - survey.

text.p: Hong Kong is set to lose its position as the country with the best business environment, according to a new ranking produced by the Economist Intelligence Unit (EIU).
Hong Kong, due to come under Chinese rule on July 1, will tumble from the top spot it held in the years 1992 to 1996 to 14th place in 1997 to 2001, the survey said.
The Netherlands will rise to first place from third, while Britain will retain its second place ranking.

The model, called the global business environment rankings, evaluates prospects for the next five years as well measuring the preceding five for 58 countries in 66 indicators. The survey includes indicators measuring macroeconomic and political environments, policy towards free enterprise, foreign investment policy and infrastructure.
Hong Kong's fall is attributable to political factors, according to the EIU.
"There is considerable risk that China will not fully honour its promises and we expect a steady increase in corruption and erosion of the rule of law," said Laza Kekic, senior economist at the EIU.
Particular areas of concern for Hong Kong are an expected decline in market opportunity and the danger of China adopting a hostile stance towards private enterprise, according to Kekic.

The Netherlands gained the top position with stong rankings in all catagories, especially strong access to financing, extremely high levels of political and economic stability and an improving tax regime.
The survey found that the global business environment will improve in the next five years as a whole, "We expect a very, very strong improvement, almost without fail," Kekic said.
"The trends towards liberalisation and globalisation are irreversible," he said.
Other than Hong Kong, only one country, Columbia, is expected to have a deterioration in absolute terms of its business environment in the coming five years.
Brazil will enjoy the most significant improvement in ranking between the two periods, the EIU said, rising to 36th place from 46.
Brazil will benefit from improved macroeconomic stability and more positive policy towards privatisation and enterprise, according to the survey.
The expected success of the Brazilian government's anti-inflation Real Plan will be a major advantage, Kekic said.
North America has the highest regional rank, and is expected to have a 3.7 percent improvement in the 1997 to 2001 period.
Eastern Europe will gain the most of any single region, with a 27.1 percent improvement expected in the same period.

Among highly developed regions, Western Europe will benefit from the biggest gain, at 8.1 percent, with trends towards liberalisation and deregulation expected to lead to improvements for most European Union member states.
The United States' business environment ranking will rise to by one place to five in the 1997 to 2001 period.
In 58th place is Iraq, which has retained its grasp on last from the preceding period.
- James Saft, London Newsroom +171 542 2734
